tokyo-kyoto.s: Kinosaki Onsen (seven public bathhouses in one walkable town, since 720 CE); ryokan with private spring baths (onsen)

costa-rica.s: Arenal Volcano hot springs around La Fortuna, several separate properties, river-fed thermal pools (geothermal spa)

azores.s: Terra Nostra Park iron-rich thermal pool in Furnas, since 1780 (geothermal spa); volcanic steam vents used for the Cozido das Furnas stew

ecuadorian-andes.s: Termas de Papallacta, about 90 minutes from Quito at 10,660 ft (geothermal spa and natural pools)

chilean-lake-district.s: Termas Geométricas near Pucón, 17 slate-lined pools fed by more than 60 natural springs (natural outdoor pools)

budapest.s: Széchenyi (one of Europe's largest bath complexes, outdoor pools open through winter since 1963); Rudás and Király, Ottoman-era baths from the 1500s (geothermal spa)

north-island.s: Rotorua's Polynesian Spa, including the Priest's Bath (since the 1870s-80s) (geothermal spa); natural geothermal creeks nearby

iceland.s: Blue Lagoon and other geothermal lagoons (geothermal spa); the Secret Lagoon and river pools such as Reykjadalur (natural outdoor pools)

taiwan.s: Beitou, reachable by MRT from Taipei; Jiaoxi's outdoor springs in Yilan (onsen style)

banff.s: Banff Upper Hot Springs on Sulphur Mountain, the highest hot spring in Canada, 100-104 F year-round, whose 1883 discovery led to the first national park

tuscany.s: Saturnia's free natural sulphur pools, Cascate del Mulino, a constant 99 F year-round (natural pools); the Terme di Saturnia resort (geothermal spa)

hokkaido.s: Rotenburo outdoor baths steaming in real snow; Noboribetsu's large onsen town (onsen and geothermal spa)

tbilisi-caucasus.s: Abanotubani's domed brick bathhouses over natural sulfur springs, a founding legend dating to the 5th century (indoor baths, open year-round)

atacama.s: Termas de Puritama, eight geothermal pools in a canyon outside San Pedro de Atacama, long sacred to the Atacameño people (natural pools)

aspen.s: Penny Hot Springs, a roadside soak on the Crystal River about 45 minutes away; Conundrum Hot Springs, an 8.5-mile backcountry hike needing an overnight permit (natural pools)

yellowstone.s: Chico Hot Springs, a working resort 30-40 minutes outside the park's north entrance in Montana (geothermal spa); the Boiling River inside the park has been closed since the 2022 floods

swissalps.s: Leukerbad, the largest thermal resort in the Alps, used since Roman times; outdoor pools ringed by snow-capped peaks (geothermal spa)

queenstown.s: Onsen Hot Pools on the Shotover (heated, treated water, not a natural spring); the nearest natural hot spring is Hanmer Springs, about four hours away

peru.s: Aguas Calientes at the base of Machu Picchu; Cocalmayo on the Salkantay route; La Calera in Colca Canyon, fed by the Cotallaulli volcano (a stopover, not a reason to plan a trip)

argentine-lake-district.s: Termas de Copahue near the Chilean border, recognized by the WHO for its sulphuric mud and thermal treatments; the access road is closed by snow from about May to November

dolomites.s: Terme Dolomia in Val di Fassa, Trentino's only sulphur spring (first documented 1493); Bagni Vecchi di Bormio, a 1,000-year-old pool built into a Roman tunnel

kyrgyzstan.s: Altyn Arashan ('Golden Spa') near Karakol, rich in radon and hydrogen sulfide, nearly every guesthouse with its own pool; reachable only June to September

chamonix.s: Les Thermes de Saint-Gervais, natural spring water at about 102 F, bathing there since at least the 14th century (Chamonix's own spa uses heated water, not a spring)

uyuni.s: Termas de Polques beside Laguna Salada near the Salvador Dali Desert geysers, over 14,110 ft, a fixed stop on the multi-day 4x4 tours (natural pools)

jordan.s: Ma'in Hot Springs between Madaba and the Dead Sea, a waterfall cascading into natural thermal pools Herod the Great reportedly used; summers top 104 F

rocky-mountain.s: Hot Sulphur Springs Resort, about 30 minutes from the park's west entrance near Grand Lake (there is no hot spring inside the park)

greenland.s: Uunartoq's hot spring on an uninhabited island in South Greenland, used since Norse settlers about 1,000 years ago; reachable only by organized boat tour June to September (natural pool)
